item.title: The rise and fall of DAOstack: lessons for decentralized autonomous organizations

findings.finding: Mixed-methods study of 92 DAOstack organizations: mainly small, short-lived DAOs; governance model functional, economic incentives ineffective; interviews report power imbalance from token ownership and reputation and cost and complexity of voting. item.title: 1Hive/conviction-voting-app ConvictionVoting.sol (commit 27df568, 2021-11-05; repo last pushed 2023-01-24)

findings.finding: Conviction is a first-order recursion on staked tokens: y(t) = a^t * y(0) + x * (1 - a^t) / (1 - a), with a = decay / D, D = 10,000,000, t in blocks since the last record. Stake x held forever converges to x / (1 - a).
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Conviction formula: a^t * y(0) + x * (1 - a^t) / (1 - a)

findings.finding: Passing threshold for a request is rho * totalStaked / (1 - a) / (beta - requested/funds)^2, where totalStaked is floored at minThresholdStakePercentage of the stake token's total supply. Equivalent closed form: the stake that must be held on a proposal until conviction saturates is rho * S / (beta - requested/funds)^2, which diverges as the request approaches beta times the funds. The contract reverts for requests at or above maxRatio times funds (ERROR_AMOUNT_OVER_MAX_RATIO).
findings.exactSourceLanguage: threshold = weight * totalStaked * D ** 2 * funds ** 2 / (D - decay) / (maxRatio * funds - requestedAmount * D) ** 2

findings.finding: executeProposal is permissionless once conviction exceeds the threshold; it transfers the requested amount from the funds manager to the beneficiary.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: require(proposal.convictionLast > calculateThreshold(requestedAmount), ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_CONVICION);

findings.finding: The threshold denominator uses the larger of actually staked tokens and a fraction of total supply, so a small active stake cannot lower the bar below that floor.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: return totalStaked < minTotalStake ? minTotalStake : totalStaked;

findings.finding: Each voter can stake on at most ten proposals at once.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: uint64 public constant MAX_STAKED_PROPOSALS = 10;

findings.finding: Stake is bound to the token balance through a token-manager hook: transferring tokens away withdraws stake first from inactive, then from active proposals, so a voter cannot move tokens and keep their conviction.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: if (newBalance < totalVoterStake[_from]) {

findings.finding: Settings (decay, maxRatio, weight, minThresholdStakePercentage), the funds manager and the price oracle are changeable by holders of the Aragon UPDATE_SETTINGS_ROLE; the app also has PAUSE_CONTRACT_ROLE and CANCEL_PROPOSALS_ROLE and a CHALLENGE_ROLE for the Agreements dispute module.

README example initialization: decay 0.9999599 (documented as a conviction half-time of 3 days; the formula gives 3.0 days at 15-second blocks and 1.0 day at 5-second blocks), maxRatio 0.2, rho 0.002, minThresholdStakePercentage 0.2. README states the code is unaudited.

findings.finding: BancorFormula prices by connector weight w in ppm: purchase return = supply * ((1 + deposit / connectorBalance)^(w / 1,000,000) - 1); at weight 100% it is linear (supply * deposit / balance). findings.finding: The Tap module limits how fast funds leave the reserve to a beneficiary: a rate per block, a floor under which the reserve cannot fall, and bounded increases to the rate and decreases to the floor, so the community cannot drain the reserve faster than a stated rate.

item.title: Commons-Stack/augmented-tbc-design: parameters and math of the augmented bonding curve (commit 80dc175, 2021-07-16)

findings.finding: Design tool converts four user parameters (Hatch raise d0, commons tribute theta, hatch price p0, open price p1) to curve parameters: kappa = p1/p0/(1-theta); initial reserve R0 = (1-theta)*d0; initial supply S0 = d0/p0; V0 = S0^kappa / R0. The invariant is R = S^kappa / V0, so reserve is a power function of supply and the spot price is dR/dS.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: const k = p1 / p0 / (1 - theta); // Invariant power kappa (.)

findings.finding: Entry and exit are taxed: theta of the Hatch raise goes to the Funding Pool and the rest to the collateral pool; an exit tribute is deducted on every burn and goes to the Funding Pool (example: 10% exit tribute, burner gets 0.9 DAI per token at a price of 1 DAI).
findings.exactSourceLanguage: The percentage that goes to the Funding Pool when token holders 'sell' by burning their token at the price determined by the ABC.

findings.finding: Hatch tokens vest on a half-life schedule after a cliff; the design tool computes a floor price from unvested hatch tokens ('Lockup Curve') and runs a 52-week simulation that the tool states is not a cadCAD simulation.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: This chart shows a 52 week simulation of discrete transactions interacting with the Augmented Bonding Curve.

findings.finding: The design tool's README is two lines; the repository carries no empirical comparison of simulated and deployed outcomes.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Experiment and test augmented token bonding curves, part of the Commons Stack

A Yes vote authorizes two follow-on proposals (technical and operational plan; treasury distribution) and a Snapshot vote was opened 2025-07-30 in the tecommons.eth space.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Over the past 18 months, TEC has transitioned from a vibrant, early-stage coordination experiment to a quieter, lower-velocity commons. Despite several attempts to revitalize engagement and token utility, participation has slowed, governance activity has declined, and the value proposition for the $TEC token has become increasingly unclear.

findings.finding: A commenter asked on 2025-08-12 whether the vote complied with the TEC Covenant's advice-process and on/off-chain voting rules; the proposer replied that the near-unanimity of participants returning to the forum for the first time in years was sufficient.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: with the near unanimity of participants coming to the forums for the first time in years calling in favour of a structured winddown was more than sufficient to come to a vote on this proposal

item.title: TEC Shutdown Proposal (forum.tecommons.org topic 1520, read via Wayback Machine)

findings.finding: Figures given in the shutdown plan: the TEC funded $433,316 in direct grants and its Gitcoin grants-round collaboration catalyzed $250,000 more; most of the original community moved on in late 2021; a sunset budget of $52,671 (severance and backpay $27,171, a $10,000 retrospective analysis grant to the Bonding Curve Research Group on the augmented bonding curve, conviction voting and the Praise system, $10,500 sunsetting operations, $5,000 claims contract); the TEC brand is retired.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Since launch, the TEC has funded $433,316 in direct grants to promising token engineering projects.

findings.finding: The plan's own account: most of the original community left in late 2021 and a small team that stayed ran grants programs largely without drawing on the common pool for two years.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Their innovative grants programs generated real awareness for token engineering, and they did this largely without touching the Common Pool for the last two years.

item.title: TEC Token Sunset (forum.tecommons.org topic 1531, read via Wayback Machine)

findings.finding: Final implementation plan (2025-12-02): replace the bonding curve with a minimal claims contract; claim amount per address is the lower of the TEC balance on 2025-07-23 (when the sunset was announced) and the balance at dissolution, to prevent last-minute speculation; two-token payout (rETH and DAI); a roughly six-month claim window after which unclaimed funds go to giv.eth; the governance vote withdraws the rETH from the ABC to the common pool and burns TEC held by the common pool.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: the amount each address can claim will be based on: the LOWER of: (1) TEC balance held on July 23, 2025 (when the sunset plan was publicly announced), or (2) TEC balance at the dissolution date

item.title: Financial Analysis of the TEC (forum.tecommons.org topic 1322, read via Wayback Machine)

findings.exactSourceLanguage: However, at launch, the entry tributes started at 22%, while the exit tributes were initially set at 2%, and these percentages gradually evolved over time.

item.title: Community Advice Process on TEC Migration to Optimism (forum.tecommons.org topic 1294, read via Wayback Machine)

findings.finding: Reasons given for moving the TEC from Gnosis to Optimism: easier TEC acquisition (buying required xDAI wrapped as wxDAI), access to capital and DeFi, reduced xDAI/DAI reliance, and Optimism's funding of public goods; Commons Stack had received an Optimism grant to port Aragon client and the ABC to Optimism. Celeste, the Aragon dispute arbitrator, does not exist on Optimism, so the migrated DAO uses Tao Voting with Guardians who can veto proposals.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Celeste, the arbitration method for proposal dispute, does not exist on Optimism.

findings.finding: The advice request proposed moving Common and Reserve pool assets through 5/7 multisigs; the TEC announced the migration complete on 2023-12-19 with rETH as new reserve currency.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Now, on OP Mainnet, the ABC is using Rocket Pool ETH (rETH) as collateral.

item.title: Fairmint/c-org reference implementation of Continuous Organizations: README, SPECIFICATIONS.md and contracts (commit 781d1ed, 2023-09-05)

findings.finding: Two-curve design: buy curve is linear price in supply (tokens bought for amount c: x = sqrt(2c/buy_slope + supply^2) - supply); sell curve is derived from the buyback reserve with sell_slope = 2 * buyback_reserve / (total_supply + burnt_supply)^2, so selling returns the reserve share rather than the buy price. Only investment_reserve of each investment stays in the buyback reserve; the rest goes to the beneficiary.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: sell_slope=(2*buyback_reserve)/((total_supply+burnt_supply)^2)

findings.finding: The beneficiary pays revenue into the reserve with pay(): revenue_commitment of the amount enters the reserve and mints FAIR to payers; the beneficiary's own purchases are 100 percent funneled into the reserve. Closing requires the beneficiary to escrow an exit fee equal to total_supply*(total_supply+burnt_supply)*buy_slope - buyback_reserve.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: To close the c-org contract, the `beneficiary` needs to pay an `exit_fee = total_supply*(total_supply+burnt_supply)*buy_slope - buyback_reserve`.

findings.finding: A control address (recommended multisig) can update beneficiary, fee, minimum investment, whitelist and revenue commitment; revenue commitment can be raised but never lowered; an ERC-1404-style whitelist contract enforces lock-ups and transfer restrictions.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: To protect investors, it is important to note that the revenue commitment can be increased but can never be decreased.

findings.finding: The repository's own README states the whitepaper dates to 2018, that Fairmint moved on from the CSO design to the CAFE, the Rolling SAFE and the Community SAFE, and that the c-org-abi package lists only DAI and USDC mainnet addresses (no deployed c-org instance).

item.title: Continuous Organizations: Aligning stakeholders' financial interests in the Digital Economy, whitepaper v1.2 (C-ORG/whitepaper)

findings.finding: Defines the Continuous Securities Offering: an organization funnels a fixed percentage of realized revenues into a Decentralized Autonomous Trust whose bonding curve has distinct buy and sell functions (the revenue-based bonding curve), issuing FAIR securities that are a claim on the DAT's cash reserve and not on ownership or governance.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: A _Continuous Securities Offering_ (_CSO_) is a novel way for organizations to receive financing without releasing any equity or any governance rights.

findings.finding: Investment funding is deliberately not held in the reserve: with investment reserve I = 10%, an investor's 10 ETH sends 9 ETH to the organization and keeps 1 ETH in the reserve.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: if I=10% then the _DAT_ will transfer 9 ETH to the organization's wallet and will keep 1 ETH in its cash reserve

item.title: commons-stack/praise (General Magic), packages/api quantification service and README (commit 31bd9b5, 2024-10-14)

findings.finding: Praise is an off-chain (MongoDB, Discord bot) community system: members praise each other, designated quantifiers score each praise, and a praise item's score is the average of its completed quantifications; a dismissed quantification scores 0 and a duplicate takes a score derived from the original praise.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Calculate the composite score by averaging the scores of all completed quantifications

findings.finding: Users listed in the README: Token Engineering Commons, Commons Stack, Giveth and Gnosis; the same repository carries database backups for Giveth (2023-06-01) and praise.giveth.io (2023-06-14).
